cards.text: Josiah, king of Judah, has set the temple in order. Friend, I've got ONE little bakery and I STILL can't find my spatula. After all this, Neco, king of Egypt, marches up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates.

cards.question: Neco king of Egypt is on the march to Carchemish. What does King Josiah do?

answers.text: He goes out to confront Neco
He sends Neco a gift of gold
He stays in Jerusalem to pray

cards.text: Neco sends messengers to Josiah, and they open with a question: “What is the issue between you and me, O king of Judah?” Me? When I've got a message, I just yell it at the oven.

cards.question: Neco's message tells Josiah that Neco has not come against him today.
Neco tells Josiah he's on his way to fight another dynasty. What does Neco say God has told him to do?

cards.text: Then Neco ends with a warning: “So stop opposing God, who is with me, or He will destroy you!” Friend, that is NOT a message you leave on read.

cards.question: After Neco's warning, Josiah turns away from Neco.

cards.text: Instead, Josiah disguises himself to engage Neco in battle. Me? NO disguise on earth could hide this mustache.

cards.question: Josiah won't listen to Neco's warning. But whose mouth did those words really come from?

cards.text: Josiah goes to fight Neco on the Plain of Megiddo. There the archers shoot King Josiah.

cards.question: After the archers shoot him, Josiah tells his servants to keep fighting without him.

cards.text: Josiah says, “Take me away, for I am badly wounded!” His servants take him out of his chariot and put him in his second chariot.

cards.question: Josiah's servants bring him to ___, and that's where he dies.

cards.text: Josiah is buried in the tomb of his fathers. I think this one hurts.

cards.question: King Josiah is buried in the tomb of his fathers. Who mourns for him?

answers.text: Only the priests in the temple

cards.text: Then Jeremiah, a prophet (Jeremiah 1:5), laments over Josiah. When this was written, the male and female singers were still reciting laments over him.

cards.question: The singers' laments over Josiah are established as a ___ for Israel.

cards.text: And those laments are written down in the Book of Laments.
The rest of Josiah's acts, from beginning to end, and his deeds of loving devotion according to the Law of the LORD are written down too. Loving devotion. Friend, that's a good way to be remembered.

cards.question: The rest of King Josiah's acts are written in another book. Which one?

answers.text: The Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah
The Book of the Wars of the LORD
